case_name: Radhu v State Of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State Of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

14 September 2007
Appeal (crl.) 624 of 2005
The Judgment was delivered by : R. V. Raveendran, J.
1. facts: On 28.1.1991 at about 8 p.m., prosecutrix Sumanbai, went to a shop for purchasing some groceries.
When she entered Gyarsibai's house, her son Radhu who was in the room came out, dragged her inside the room and confined her in the room during the entire night.
During the night, he sexually assaulted her by inserting his penis in her vagina twice.
She went back to her house and told her mother Lalithabai (PW-4) about the incident.
Sumanbai was sent to Dr. Vandana (PW-8), a lady surgeon in the Main Hospital, Khargone for examination.
Radhu was arrested on 19.2.1991 and sent to Khargone Hospital for medical examination.
issues: Whether the accused were falsely implicated by Sumanbai at the instance of her father who was indebted to Radhu's father Nathu, to avoid repayment of the debt.

Whether the prosecution case that the prosecutrix was gagged by Radhu, that the prosecutrix was confined in his house during the entire night by use of force by Radhu, that she was freed by Radhu only the next morning, becomes false.
petitioner_arguments: The accused were falsely implicated by Sumanbai at the instance of her father who was indebted to Radhu's father Nathu, to avoid repayment of the debt.
The medical evidence showed that there was no injury on the private parts of Sumanbai and that the rupture of hymen was old.

The discrepancies in the evidence, absence of corroboration, the close relationship (the prosecutrix described Radhu as her maternal uncle, as Radhu's parents were Kaka and Baba of Sumanbai's mother) and the manner in which the incident is alleged to have taken place, clearly demonstrated that it was a false charge.
respondent_arguments: The concurrent findings recorded by the trial court and High Court were based on the evidence of the prosecutrix and that no corroboration was required when the testimony of the prosecutrix was clear and convincing.
There was nothing to show that the prosecutrix had falsely implicated the accused.
court_reasoning: A finding of guilt in a case of rape, can be based on the uncorroborated evidence of the prosecutrix.
The very nature of offence makes it difficult to get direct corroborating evidence.

If the victim of rape states on oath that she was forcibly subjected to sexual intercourse, her statement will normally be accepted, even if it is uncorroborated, unless the material on record requires drawing of an inference that there was consent or that the entire incident was improbable or imaginary.
holding: The appeal by special leave filed by the accused is dismissed. The judgment and order passed by the High Court affirming the conviction and sentence of the first accused Radhu are upheld.
